name: Antonio Conte
scopeNote: Narrowed again on 2026-11-04 (user decision): only Chelsea 2016-18 and Inter 2019-21 are counted; Juventus, Italy and Napoli sources stay in the file as context with verified false. Narrowed on 2026-11-04 (user decision): only Juventus 2011-14, Chelsea 2016-18 and Inter 2019-21 are counted. The Italy national team (2014-16) and Napoli (2024-26) spells are excluded; their sources stay in the file as context with verified false. Counted spells: Juventus 2011-14, Italy 2014-16, Chelsea 2016-18, Inter 2019-21, Napoli 2024-26 (ended by mutual consent on 4 June 2026, so no longer ongoing). Style is a back three with wing-backs (3-5-2 at Juventus, Italy and Inter; 3-4-3 / 3-4-2-1 at Chelsea 2016/17 after starting with a back four), with a pressing, man-oriented / chain-reaction marking rather than a pure zonal block; sources also call the 'counter-attacking' label an oversimplification. Napoli tactical coverage is thin (only 4-3-3 mentioned by Conte himself in Aug 2025). Spell start dates other than Napoli's end and Inter's end are not in the digests (see openQuestions). Tottenham 2021-23, Bari 2007-09, Siena 2010-11 and Atalanta/Arezzo are excluded. Excluded early spells (Arezzo, Bari, Atalanta, Siena) have year-only dates from memory.
openQuestions: Exact spell dates were not found in any mined page and come from the researcher's memory: Juventus 2011-05-31 to 2014-07-15, Italy 2014-08-14 to 2016-07-03, Chelsea 2016-07-01 to 2018-07-13, Inter 2019-05-31 to 2021-05-26, Napoli 2024-06-05 to 2026-06-04. Verified in the digests: Napoli end 2026-06-04 (Corriere dello Sport), Inter end 2021-05-26 only from a URL seen in search results (inter.it communique), Juventus resignation 'May 2014' per 90min/SI (conflicts with memory of July 2014), Napoli scudetto 23 May 2025, Supercoppa 22 Dec 2025.

Tottenham 2021-23 excluded: no title, left by mutual consent before the end of the second season, and no Tottenham page was mined (Coaches' Voice zonal-marking page describes a zonal back five with Kane withdrawn, but it is outside the counted spells). Could be added if the user wants a recognisable-style spell counted; Coaches' Voice, Analytics FC and Mastermind pages exist.

Bari 2007-09 (Serie B title, 4-2-4 with wingers pushing up) and Siena 2010-11 (promotion) excluded: only secondary coverage (90min/SI, FourFourTwo) and the style (4-2-4) was abandoned for the back three.

Marking label: Spielverlagerung describes Italy-Spain at Euro 2016 as a 'rigid man-marking scheme' while SoccerTutor describes Juventus's 'chain-reaction marking' (a zonal-leaning, pass-the-responsibility system with a man-oriented press). Neither is pure zonal; a Chelsea/Inter marking source was not found.

Napoli 2024-26 has no tier A-B tactical source in the digests (CBS, Sofascore, Scouting for Success, Mastermind not readable); Inter 2019-21 tactical analysis (Mastermind) was a 403. Set-pieces have no verified in-period fact.
The Goal.com page contains the quote 'If the manager doesn't want to see the bad situation, he loses the changing room' without date or primary source; left out of statedView for lack of a date.
Goal.com generic paragraphs (counter-attack label, direct build-up) are undated and not used as verified evidence.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] This tactical analysis covers Conte's 3-5-2 in detail, from Pirlo's deep playmaker role to the wing-backs' asymmetric positioning.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] The key innovation was what Conte called "the diamond at the back." When Pirlo dropped between the three centre-backs, Juventus formed a four-man build-up structure that gave them numerical superiority against almost any pressing system. (...) Conte demanded patient build-up rather than rushed forward play. The team gradually pushed players higher while keeping the diamond intact, controlling tempo and waiting for the right moment to accelerate.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] Against a three-man defence, the forwards pressed aggressively to force play wide, trapping the opposition on the touchline and winning the ball high. (...) Against a four-man defence, they were more passive: blocking lanes through midfield and waiting for the right moment to press.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] The most sophisticated piece of Juventus's defence was chain-reaction marking. When Asamoah pushed up to press the opposition right-back, Chiellini stepped out to take the winger, and Marchisio dropped to cover Chiellini's space, ready for a potential double-up. Players drilled these transitions until they were instinctive.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] The chain-reaction marking only worked because every player communicated through every defensive transition. The positions matter, but the talking is what makes the system function.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] Lichtsteiner and Asamoah gave the 3-5-2 its width, and their different profiles created asymmetric attacking patterns. Asamoah was the attack-minded wing-back, pushing high up the left. Lichtsteiner was more conservative on the right, providing defensive insurance and overlapping only when the situation demanded it.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] The signature pattern under Conte saw players receive between the opposition's midfield and defensive lines. When Pirlo got the ball in the centre, the strong-side attacking midfielder dropped, the wing-back on that side pushed forward, and the weak-side midfielder made a forward run to receive between the lines.

sources.title: Juventus Tactics: Conte, Allegri and the 3-5-2 Dynasty
sources.evidence: [Outside the counted spells, kept as context] Tevez excelled at dropping deep to link with midfielders. Llorente's aerial presence made him the target for crosses, while his movement in the box opened space for others.
